findings.evidence: Lines 328–330 introduce all three equivariance hypotheses; lines 337–410 use `hequiv₁` and `hequiv₂` only as witnesses passed to `explicitCup10`, `explicitCup01`, `explicitCup11`, `explicitCup02`, and `explicitCup20`. For example, lift `b₁` along `SB.proj`; then `μ₁ (g • a₁) (g • b₁) = μ (g • SA.incl a₁) (g • b) = g • μ₁ a₁ b₁`, and the analogous argument lifting `a₂` along `SA.proj` proves equivariance of `μ₂`.
findings.fix: Remove `hequiv₁` and `hequiv₂` from the public hypotheses and derive both locally from `hequiv`, `hincl`, `hproj`, and `SA.proj_surjective`/`SB.proj_surjective` for use by the cup products.
findings.issue: `hequiv₁` and `hequiv₂` are redundant assumptions in all three new declarations: their equivariance follows by lifting through the surjective projections and rewriting with `hincl`/`hproj`, equivariance of `incl`/`proj`, and `hequiv`.

summary: All three adjointness theorems require two equivariance hypotheses that already follow from the central pairing’s equivariance and the compatibility equations.
